solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Flexible head of department is the last to junk redundant hardware

parts.note: flexible means bendy or limp, i.e. floppy

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept
the last letter of the following word is wanted, its final character

explanation.surface: A pliable department chief is the final person to throw out obsolete computer kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of' takes D from department and 'the last to' takes K from junk.
explanation.definitionFit: The bendable storage disc is obsolete computer equipment, no longer made or used.

clue.text: Ordinary iron ship

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A plain iron-hulled vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordinary' is a heraldic term here, not the adjective it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry an ordinary is one of the simple bold charges, and the horizontal band across a shield is one of them.

clue.text: What accountant may be required to show police

definitions.text: What accountant may be required to show
definitions.meaning: an accountant justifying expenses may have to produce a past invoice
British slang for the police force

explanation.surface: An accountant forced to produce evidence for the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A past invoice is literally an aged account, and the same phrase is British slang for the constabulary.

clue.text: Force a rugby player to cheat

parts.note: to force or drag something is to pull it
a flanker is a forward on the side of the rugby scrum

explanation.surface: Coercing a rugby forward into foul play.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom means to trick or deceive someone, so it is a phrase for cheating.

clue.text: Poor organisation arrived to cover maiden in distress

indicators.note: to cover for someone is to stand in for them, so one piece replaces another

parts.note: distress or alarm is dismay
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over
ARR is the timetable abbreviation for arrived

explanation.surface: Someone arrives to rescue a damsel in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cover' means ARR stands in for the M of DISMAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of confusion or untidiness is a lack of order, hence bad arrangement.

clue.text: Fashionable small pad

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a nappy is an absorbent pad for a baby (British for diaper)

explanation.surface: A trendy little flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pad' pretends to be a home; it is a baby's nappy.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy dressing is smart and stylish, as in a dapper outfit.

clue.text: Run about and spout

parts.note: C is circa, Latin for about
the lip of a jug is its pouring spout

explanation.surface: A jug's spout described in terms of liquid running around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To move at speed is to go at a fast pace, a sense of the verb meaning hurry along.

clue.text: Unsheathe something electric, perhaps up in shelter

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to unsheathe a sword is to draw it
an electric eel is one example of the fish

explanation.surface: Drawing out an electrical item while taking cover.
explanation.definitionFit: The side away from the wind is the protected side, so being there is being sheltered.

clue.text: Sorry to stop punishment over harbouring a group of soldiers

indicators.note: harbouring means holding within, so a letter goes inside
over means turned over, so the letters run backwards
to stop a hole is to plug it, so one word is placed within another

parts.note: a strap is a leather belt used for beating
sorry in the sense of pitiful or poor

explanation.surface: Apologising to halt a beating over sheltering a band of troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorry' here is the adjective meaning pitiful, not an apology; 'to stop', 'over' and 'harbouring' each signal a step, applied in that order.
explanation.definitionFit: Airborne troops form a body of fighters dropped by parachute.

clue.text: Cleaner imposes upon grandma?

parts.note: to saddle someone with a task is to impose it on them
a grandmother is perhaps an OAP, an old age pensioner

explanation.surface: A domestic help who burdens an elderly grandmother.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a product for cleaning and conditioning leather tack.

clue.text: Perhaps a drop of drink right at the end

indicators.note: at the end places the next piece after the rest

parts.note: tea is a drink

explanation.surface: Maybe a little drink taken right at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop' looks like a measure of drink; it is a teardrop.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop from the eye is one example of the droplet described.

clue.text: Discreet observer following development of Ely town hall

indicators.note: development implies a change in form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unobtrusive watcher after the redevelopment of a Cambridgeshire civic building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development of' is the anagram signal. Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone watching unnoticed, like an insect on a vertical surface.

clue.text: Old car examination

definitions.meaning: the Vauxhall model of that name was a British family car of the 1960s-70s
short for ... voce, an oral exam

explanation.surface: An MOT test for a vintage motor.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a discontinued Vauxhall saloon and an oral university test.

clue.text: With which you'd drive off large insect

definitions.text: With which you'd drive off large insect

parts.note: to drive off attackers is to repel them
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: The stuff you'd use to see off a big bug.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay; this spelling is a variant of the usual ending in -ent.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect deterrent is a substance used to keep bugs away.

clue.text: What students must do to get at least this?

definitions.text: What students must do to get at least this?

parts.words: What students must do to get at least this?
parts.note: a student must succeed in the exams, then gets the lowest university award, one without honours

explanation.surface: Asking what students must achieve for a minimum qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: The first word is what a student must do; the whole is the minimum degree that results.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the ordinary bachelor's award, granted without honours, the lowest grade of graduation.

clue.text: Everybody getting unequivocal signal to come out?

parts.note: everybody means all
unequivocal means plain or clear

explanation.surface: Everyone receiving an unmistakable cue to emerge.
explanation.definitionFit: The siren after an air raid told people it was safe to leave shelters.

clue.text: Violent criminal loves to cause misfortune

parts.note: a hood is a hoodlum or gangster
love is zero in tennis, O, so loves gives two of them

explanation.surface: A thug's affections bring bad luck.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to jinx or bring bad luck upon someone.

clue.text: Caught wicked woman framing North American body

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: framing means surrounding something like a picture frame

parts.note: an ogress is a cruel female monster

explanation.surface: A villainous woman arrested for setting up a transatlantic organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North' looks like part of the definition but supplies N.
explanation.definitionFit: The US legislature, the Senate and House together, is a political assembly.

clue.text: Colour of girl is returning

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl's hue is coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an earthy brownish-yellow pigment named after an Italian city, a shade of paint.

clue.text: Jewish sectarian once hiding cold character

indicators.note: hiding means concealing within, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: the Essenes were an ancient Jewish ascetic sect
C is short for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: An ancient sect member concealing an aloof personality.
explanation.definitionFit: The core nature of a thing is its intrinsic quality or character.

clue.text: Cheers when son goes from shop floor to the board?

definitions.text: from shop floor to the board?

indicators.note: goes means departs, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: a toast meaning drink up

explanation.surface: A toast when a son's career rises from worker to director.
explanation.definitionFit: A management approach starting with workers and moving upward reverses the usual hierarchy.

clue.text: Cremate injured animal

indicators.note: injured means damaged or knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An order to burn a hurt creature.
explanation.definitionFit: This African mongoose relative is a small burrowing mammal; the -cat spelling is a variant.

clue.text: Ducks going under cove find seabird

indicators.note: in a down clue, going under places this piece below the one before

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a man, a gent
a duck is a score of zero in cricket, O, so ducks gives two

explanation.surface: Waterfowl diving beneath a bay discover a marine bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cove' looks like a bay but is a chap.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentoo is a penguin species, a flightless marine bird.

clue.text: Gourmand, skipping starter, with urge for festive treat

indicators.note: skipping the starter means leaving out the opening letter

parts.note: a gourmand is someone who feasts
to urge on is to egg on

explanation.surface: A glutton missing the first course but keen for a holiday delicacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skipping starter' drops the F of FEASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocolate confection given at the spring holiday is a seasonal sweet.

clue.text: Former community manager

parts.note: ex means former
EC stands for European Community

explanation.surface: An ex-boss of a local group.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for executive, a business manager or senior officer.

clue.text: Hollowed indentations on mid-section of skeleton key

indicators.note: hollowed means emptied out, so only the outside letters remain
the mid-section is the central pair of letters

explanation.surface: Indented grooves cut into the middle of a skeleton key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skeleton key' suggests a lock; 'key' alone means a low island.
explanation.definitionFit: A key or cay is a small low island, as in the Florida Keys.

clue.text: Manage to introduce English character

indicators.note: to introduce is to come before, so this piece leads the next

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: Managing to present an English personality.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter of the old Germanic alphabet is a written symbol.

clue.text: Ones having to hide note following extreme remarks

indicators.note: following places this piece after the one before

parts.note: utter means total or extreme

indicators.note: hide means conceal within, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: aces are ones in cards or dice

explanation.surface: Persons forced to conceal a message after outrageous comments.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken statements or things said are synonyms for comments.

clue.text: Take first one from a number divisible by two

indicators.note: take away the first one, the opening letter

parts.note: seven is a number

explanation.surface: A maths instruction to subtract one from a number divisible by two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take first one from' drops the S of SEVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An integer with no remainder on halving is the mathematical meaning.

clue.text: My landlord almost hides extremely strange hidden habit?

indicators.note: hides means conceals inside, so letters go within

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation like my!

indicators.note: almost means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a letter is one who lets property, a landlord

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Expression of surprise at a landlord's secret odd habit.
explanation.walkthrough: A letter here is one who lets property. 'almost' trims its last letter, 'extremely' picks the ends of strange, and 'hides' means the joined pieces wrap round those ends. 'habit' means clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a woman's undergarment, worn beneath clothes, so concealed attire, with habit meaning dress.
